output.brief: The rise in recorded falls at the two homes is real in the figures, but the evidence does not show the rota caused it. Both homes switched to the incident app on 1 July, the same quarter the count jumped. Staff say falls with no injury were under-written before, and a check of old handover notes found at least three unreported falls in a sample of Q2 weeks. Most of the rise is no-harm and 'found on floor' events, which fits better recording. Per bed day, both homes' Q3 rates sit inside their long-run range, and other homes have had similar one-quarter jumps that reversed. However, a real rise of around 40% would take two to three quarters to show, so I can't rule out harm from the rota. Frailer admissions and the GP medication changes are untested. Nobody has call-bell timings from before June, so the claim that bells are answered slower is unproven. I'm moderately confident. Recommended: don't revert or halt the rollout now, and don't discipline staff or withdraw the app. Keep the pilot under its pause criteria. Show falls as rates with the reporting change marked. Start manual sampling of night call-bell response times. Review admissions mix and medication changes. Decide on the rollout at a dated review in late January with Q4 data.
